title: CS pocket signal briefing - actionable micro-requests
content:
TL;DR: This is a compact synthesis of 18 support threads + 7 account interviews (May-Jun 2026). Goal: convert compact voice signals into 6 micro-requests that are small enough for an eng sprint but high ROI for customers. Emphasis on inference economics (cost-to-quality), routing/resilience, and observability gaps customers repeatedly mentioned.

Methodology: quick triage (support severity, ARR impact, recurrentness), stitch similar language into micro-themes, validate with 2 customer interview notes, and translate into proposed fixes and owners. Not a final prioritization — intended as a routing-ready ticket list for product/eng to review.

Observed patterns (one-liners):
- Customers confuse model variant naming + fallback behavior during failures.
- Per-route cost attribution is too coarse; finance teams want token-level breakouts by model variant and cache hits.
- Streaming disconnects cause duplicate partial responses; teams want resume tokens or idempotent streaming semantics.
- Caching controls are black-boxy: clients want to opt-out of prefix caching for sensitive requests (PII).
- Dedicated customers ask for better quantization guidance per workload (embedding vs generation).
- Embedding drift: same text yields slightly different vectors over model upgrades; customers need embedding-stable upgrade paths.

Prioritized micro-requests (actionable, rough-est effort):
1) "Variant clarity & fallback explainer" (effort: 1 sprint + doc)
   - Symptom: customers surprised when hosted falls back to cheaper variant during capacity pressure, leading to bad SLAs.
   - Ask: UI + API flag to explicitly opt into or opt out of automatic fallback per-route (and email alerts when fallback happens).
   - Proposed quick fix: add query param fallback_policy: [allow, prefer, disallow] and surface recent fallback events in Console route dashboard.
   - Owner: product-hosted-api + console-and-rollouts.
   - Expected impact: reduces unexpected behavioral regressions; immediate trust boost for teams on Dedicated trials.

2) "Per-token cost trace + cache-hit taxonomy" (effort: 2 sprints)
   - Symptom: billing disputes and inability to reconcile spikes when caching/batching changes.
   - Ask: logs + CSV export that map request_id -> token_count -> model_variant -> cache_hit(true/false) -> cost_estimate.
   - Quick win: prototype a CSV output for last 7 days on Console for any route.
   - Risks: PII in logs — ensure sampling/anonymization.
   - Owner: observability + billing.

3) "Streaming resume tokens" (effort: 2 sprints)
   - Symptom: customers implementing client-side streaming must restart sessions and dedupe responses after network blips.
   - Ask: include a stable resume token (opaque string) periodically in the stream, and an API to resume from that token.
   - Alternate: idempotency keys per-chunk (but heavier).
   - Owner: serving-runtime + developer-experience.

4) "Cache opt-out per-request + sensitivity label" (effort: 1 sprint)
   - Symptom: compliance teams worried about prefix caching of PII.
   - Ask: add header "x-redwood-cache: off|session|prefix" and console policy that enforces cache-off for routes marked as "sensitive".
   - Quick enforcement: route-level default = on; allow org-admins to toggle.
   - Owner: private-deployments + platform-engineering.

5) "Quantization & perf recommendation endpoint" (effort: 2-3 sprints)
   - Symptom: Dedicated/on-prem customers unsure which quantization profile to choose; they fear quality regressions.
   - Ask: an API that accepts a small sample workload (5–20 prompts) and returns recommended profile (FP16/int8 variants) + expected latency/cost delta and a confidence score.
   - Implementation note: start with a heuristic table (model type + seq len -> profile) then progressively sample.
   - Owner: applied-ml + serving-runtime.

6) "Embedding upgrade compatibility lane" (effort: 2 sprints + eval infra)
   - Symptom: after model upgrades, embeddings shift and downstream similarity pipelines degrade.
   - Ask: an "embedding compatibility" report when a new model is promoted: pairwise cosine shift histogram, backward-compatible tag, recommended migration window.
   - Quick step: for each model in catalog, publish a reference embedding set (100 canonical sentences) and automatic diffs on new releases.
   - Owner: product-optimize + research.

Quick wins (can be shipped as docs/config changes):
- Short doc: "What happens when capacity is constrained" (console FAQ + in-app tooltip). Low effort; high reduction in support noise.
- Template: billing export CSV for top 10 routes.
- Slack alert integration for fallback events (channel + email) — plug to PagerDuty optionally.

Risk flags / unknowns:
- Billing CSV accuracy vs. rounding (finance will push back). Need payment & legal consult before shipping CSV.
- Resume tokens change runtime semantics — may complicate KV cache alignment. Serving-runtime needs to validate designs with existing cache layers.
- Quantization recommendation endpoint needs a sandbox infra to avoid leaking customer data.

Customer vignettes (short):
- "HealthTech startup" (mid-market): saw sudden drop in throughput when fallback kicked in overnight; customer engineer believed model was pinned — they had no visibility. Outcome: SLA alert but late — customer opened a CSM escalation.
- "AdTech pipeline" (high-volume): needs deterministic embeddings across weekly model upgrades for dedup pipeline. Migration currently manual and fragile.
- "Marketplace" (enterprise): blocked by compliance; wants per-request cache-off header and legal sign-off that no prefixes are stored.

Suggested next steps (immediate):
1) Product-hosted-api & Console sync (30m) to approve fallback_policy param and console exposure.
2) Observability backlog ticket to prototype billing CSV export; attach sample CSV from Sep 2025 to validate fields.
3) Schedule 1-2 spike tickets for resume token feasibility with serving-runtime (include Marco + Ling).

Metrics to watch post-shipping:
- Reduction in support tickets referencing "unexpected fallback" (target: -70% in 90 days).
- Number of routes using fallback_policy=disallow (adoption).
- Billing export disputes opened (target: down to 10% of current).
- Embedding drift alerts triggered by compatibility reports.

Notes to self / open questions:
- Is there an existing header we could reuse for cache control? (Ling to confirm).
- Legal: what language for cache-off guarantees in hosted environment? (Priya to loop in).
- Can we reuse existing telemetry (trace id mapping) for per-token CSV? Evan to check sampling limits.

Appendix (short):
- Raw signals included: 18 support threads (IDs: shared internally), 7 customer interview notes (HealthTech, AdTech, Marketplace, FinServ, Retail + 2 SMBs), 3 partner integrations feedback (k8s operator related).
- Related tickets: JIRA-CS-1987 (fallback confusion), JIRA-OBS-2122 (billing export request), JIRA-ML-3004 (quantization guidance).

Bottom line: these micro-requests are intentionally scoped to be implementable in small sprints and to unblock high-friction customer issues. Recommend product + eng pairing sessions next week to convert the top 3 into concrete tickets with acceptance criteria.

-- Aisha
(contributor: Marco, Ling, Priya)
